summary.title: codeslinger.co.uk – CHIP-8 emulation tutorial
summary.one_liner: Learn the core pieces needed to write a CHIP-8 interpreter: loading a ROM, registers, the program counter and stack, opcode fetch/decode/execute, and timers, sound and input.
takeaways: A CHIP-8 emulator needs a byte array for the loaded game, registers, a program counter and a stack.
The main loop fetches an opcode from memory, decodes it, and executes its instructions.
Timers, basic sound and keyboard input complete the system emulation.
Prior knowledge of general emulation basics is assumed; the author points to a separate emulation guide.
Useful references include the Wikipedia CHIP-8 page and the CHIP-8 instruction set documentation.
summary.summary: This page is a short CHIP-8 emulation tutorial from codeslinger.co.uk's emulation programming section. It lists what a reader needs to know before starting: reading a game into a byte array, emulating registers, program counter and stack, fetching and decoding opcodes, and handling timers, primitive sound and input. It assumes the reader has already read the author's general emulation guide. The page also lists its resources, including Wikipedia, a CHIP-8 instruction set reference and David Winter's documentation. The excerpt does not include code, so it works as an outline rather than a full walkthrough.
